ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Fig. 1, $Rt\triangle BAC$ and $Rt\triangle DAE$ are both isosceles right-angled triangles, and $AB=AC=2\sqrt{5}$, $AD=AE=2\sqrt{2}$, $\angle BAC=\angle DAE=90^\circ$. $\triangle DAE$ rotates counterclockwise around point A; connect CD. When $\tan\angle EAC=\frac{1}{3}$, find the length of CD.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $DW \perp AC$ at $W$,\\
since $\angle DAE=90^\circ$ and $\tan\angle EAC=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
thus $\angle ADW+\angle DAW=\angle DAW+\angle EAC$,\\
hence $\angle EAC=\angle ADW$,\\
in right triangle $\triangle AWD$ with $\angle AWD=90^\circ$,\\
thus $\tan\angle ADW=\frac{AW}{DW}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
assume $DW=3k$ and $AW=k$, then $(3k)^2+k^2=(2\sqrt{2})^2$,\\
hence $AW=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}$ and $DW=\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}$,\\
thus $WC=AC-AW=\frac{8\sqrt{5}}{5}$,\\
in right triangle $\triangle DWC$ with $\angle DWC=90^\circ$,\\
thus $DW^2+WC^2=DC^2$,\\
therefore, $DC=\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A is the upper common vertex of the large triangle BAC, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and AC is the side pointing from A to the lower right; the small triangle DAE also has A as its vertex, D is located inside the large triangle near A, E is to the right of A, CD is connected in the figure, and the goal is to find CD. Then reason: According to the specified coordinate method, take A as the origin, the x-axis along the direction of AC, and the positive y direction on the AC side where D is located. Because AC=2√5, C=(2√5,0). Let θ=∠EAC. It is known that tan θ=1/3, therefore one may take sin θ=1/√10, cos θ=3/√10. Also because AD⊥AE, and in the figure D is on the positive y side of AC, the components of AD relative to the AC direction are (sin θ, cos θ). AD=2√2, therefore D=(2√2·sin θ,2√2·cos θ)=(2/√5,6/√5). Thus CD²=(2√5-2/√5)²+(0-6/√5)²=(8/√5)²+(6/√5)²=64/5+36/5=20, so CD=√20=2√5.
